title: Edge POC: latency-savvy quant + prompt pipeline journal
body:
Purpose and context:
This document captures iterative experiments for a customer POC that targets an edge-hosted inference footprint (single GPU / 2x A10-ish or equivalent T4-class) with strict 250ms median latency tail for short completions (<=64 tokens). Goal is to minimize cost and memory by aggressive quantization while preserving response usefulness for the product's FAQ + action extraction use cases. This is a working lab notebook: contains raw notes, numbers, heuristics, and TODOs.

High-level constraints (customer):
- Max cold-start P95 <= 350ms, median <= 250ms for 64-token replies.
- Model must run on a single 24GB GPU in their edge appliance.
- Privacy: no external API calls; all inference local.
- Throughput target: 8 concurrent users with average request every 10s.
- Quality baseline: human-rated helpfulness >= 4/5 on 50 eval prompts (current prod baseline: 4.2).

Hardware + infra used for experiments:
- Local test machine: 1x A10-24GB (single process), Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 11.8, Triton runtime stubbed for microbenchmarks.
- Runtime: Redwood inference runtime (dev branch) with custom kernel selector, GPTQ runtime compiled.
- Measurement harness: 1000-sample synthetic trace derived from customer logs (mix of short FAQ, follow-ups, and one-shot entity extraction).

Models & quantization variants tried (short names used below):
- llama-2-7b (fp16 baseline)
- llama-2-7b-gptq-q4_0 (GPTQ 4-bit, per-channel)
- llama-2-7b-awq-nf4 (AWQ-style nf4 4-bit)
- mistral-instruct-7b-int8 (int8 fallback)
- distill-3b-llm (3b fp16 smaller model for A/B)

Key pipeline components evaluated:
1) Prompt condensing (client-side): shortens user context into system-level bullets to reduce token length to model. Implemented two heuristics: rule-based extractor and a tiny seq2seq rewriter (distill-3b) on-device.
2) Prefix/KV caching window: persistent KV cache for repeated conversation prefixes (empirically helps 30% of traces).
3) Dynamic quant routing: attempt lower-bit quant (4-bit) first, fall back to int8 only if quality regression detected by internal light-weight reranker.
4) Local reranker (distill-3b) that compares candidates from quantized and int8 runs for critical queries (costly, used only when certain heuristics trigger).

Microbenchmarks (median latency, 64 tokens, cold-warm indicated):
- llama-2-7b fp16: cold 420ms, warm 260ms (quality baseline)
- llama-2-7b-gptq-q4_0: cold 190ms, warm 120ms (note: slight degradation on factuality prompts)
- llama-2-7b-awq-nf4: cold 210ms, warm 125ms (better coherence than gptq on dialogue)
- mistral-instruct-7b-int8: cold 240ms, warm 150ms (robust but memory heavy)
- distill-3b-llm: cold 130ms, warm 90ms (good latency, weaker extraction accuracy)

Quality checks (small eval set of 50 prompts, averaged human helpfulness 1-5):
- fp16 baseline: 4.25
- gptq-q4_0: 3.95 (notable drop on code-like or multi-step arithmetic)
- awq-nf4: 4.05 (tradeoff model-dependent; better on conversational coherence)
- int8: 4.10
- distill-3b: 3.6

Observations and heuristics learned:
- GPTQ 4-bit is the best latency reduction but has the highest variance in subtle reasoning tasks. For FAQ-style retrieval-augmented generation (short answers), gptq often suffices.
- AWQ/nf4 produced slightly higher quality for conversational follow-ups; choose AWQ when dialogue quality is prioritized.
- int8 is a sensible middle ground when memory allows; it is less latency-optimized than q4 but more stable for edge cases.
- Distill 3b is useful as a fast rewriter/reranker; it can be used client-side to reduce tokens and as a cheap quality check.
- Prefix KV caching reduces average latency by ~12% for conversational sessions where prefixes repeat; implement LRU with size cap per-user.

Routing policy suggestion for POC (latency-first):
- Step 1: Apply prompt condensing locally (rule-based). If condensing reduces tokens by >=20% proceed.
- Step 2: Route to quantized 4-bit model (gptq) with short time budget (timeout 180ms).
- Step 3: If candidate fails quick heuristics (length mismatch, hallucination markers, low reranker score) or exceeds time budget, fallback to int8 variant.
- Step 4: If still unsatisfactory and query flagged as "sensitive/extraction", run distill-3b reranker comparing outputs. Return highest-scored result.

Cost/Memory tradeoffs (notes):
- GPTQ q4 weights: ~10-11GB for 7b; fits comfortably in a 24GB GPU with room for runtime scratch.
- AWQ nf4: ~11.5GB; slightly larger kernel memory.
- int8: ~14-15GB; leaves less headroom for batch/serving layers.

Edge-specific engineering notes:
- Kernel warmup: first inference is slow due to Just-in-Time kernel selection; keep a tiny warm pool process pinned to GPU to reduce cold-start tail.
- Streaming: 4-bit implementations had noisier token generation times — batching tiny concurrent requests improves efficiency but hurts p95 latency. Use dynamic batching cap tuned to concurrency.
- Quantization artifacts are often prompt-sensitive: adding a short system reminder ("Answer succinctly and verify factual claims") reduces hallucinations for q4 by ~6%.

Quick playbook (practical checklist for next customer demo):
- Prepare two artifacts: gptq-q4_0 model + int8 fallback, both loaded in same runtime.
- Implement rule-based condense module client-side (fast path).
- Add prefix-KV caching with 30s TTL for conversational flows.
- Expose a debug route that returns model choice, tokens saved, and reranker scores for first 50 requests.
- Add a background warmup process that runs a small synthetic query every 60s.

Experiment log (short entries):
- 2025-11-04: Ran batch of 1000 traces; gptq q4 reduced token cost by 3.2x vs fp16 and met median target but failed 9% of critical extraction prompts.
- 2025-11-07: Introduced prompt-condense rules; average token consumption dropped 28%, median latency improved 15%.
- 2025-11-12: Deployed AWQ variant A/B; human rating improved on dialogue cases from 3.95 to 4.05; choose AWQ for conversational POC.
- 2025-11-15: Implemented dynamic routing prototype; end-to-end p95 cold trimmed from 420ms to 340ms.

Decision log (final recommendation for POC):
- Default model: llama-2-7b-awq-nf4 for conversational-focused POC (better coherence).
- If strict 250ms median is absolute and queries are mostly short FAQs, use gptq-q4_0 with more aggressive prompt condensation + retry on int8 when flagged.
- Always keep distill-3b as a local on-device rewriter/reranker for high-value queries.

Open questions / risks:
- Some customers' prompts include code blocks and tables where q4 degrades more; need targeted eval set for those customers.
- AWQ tooling maturity: risk around edge vendor kernel compatibility. Plan: include fallback int8 image in release.
- Monitoring: define SLOs not only for latency but for quality regression (weekly sample of 200 queries scored by SMEs).

Next actions (owners):
- Ben: finalize prompt-condense rules and add as SDK snippet (due 2025-11-25).
- Marina: finish A/B evaluation against customer's 200-case doc (due 2025-11-22).
- Diego: integrate warmup microservice + dynamic batching policy (due 2025-11-30).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally experimental. Expect TODOs and raw numbers. Please append comments on the linked PR for changes to the runtime or kernels.

Appendix: small example prompts and observed failure modes
- Prompt: "Summarize this internal policy and list three actions" -> gptq shortened list, dropped caveats. AWQ preserved caveats.
- Prompt: "Extract invoice amounts from text: ..." -> gptq occasionally mis-parsed currency formats. Use int8 for extraction-heavy routes.

End of notebook.
